name: Morton/Z-order densification (locality-preserving param+optimizer reordering)
faster_gs_ref: src/Methods/FasterGS/Trainer.py:141-145 morton_ordering @ MORTON_ORDERING_INTERVAL=5000, END=15000; Model.py apply_morton_ordering via CudaUtils.MortonEncoding.morton_encode + argsort(means)
c0_status: C0 has NO morton ordering. ORIGINAL_METHOD_PROTOCOL clone/split/prune densification (config: densify_from=500, until=15000, interval=100, opacity_reset=3000). No param/optimizer reordering anywhere in C0.
classification_note: Pure memory-layout change. C0 forward is per-tile (depth)sorted (HigsNativeBackward.cu header: 'per-tile sorted'), so global morton order does NOT alter alpha-blend output => output-preserving / exact. Not bit-exact (FP kernel re-launch identical; only memory layout differs) => ALGEBRAIC_EXACT_FP_REASSOCIATED at most, but render output is bit-identical (same kernels, same math).
gate_compliance: No production CUDA modification. Microbench used pinned C0 .so READ-ONLY. Component audit + opportunity oracle gate satisfied (returned to reviewer before any CUDA mod).

method.type: NO-CUDA microbench on pinned C0 .so (zero source modification)
method.render_path: rasterize_gaussian_higs_dynamic(backward_mode=higs_native, enable_culling=True) -- identical to trainer c0 arm render_with_meta
method.design: c8_microbench3.py: interleaved A/B/A/B rounds with inverse-perm restore (apply perm, measure B, apply argsort(perm), measure A) to cancel GPU clock drift; 50 iters/round; 4-5 rounds/scene; median aggregation
method.morton_key: 3D 20-bit bit-interleaved Z-order from means; argsort; in-place permute of _xyz/_shs/_scaling/_rotation/_opacity + optimizer exp_avg/exp_avg_sq
method.e2e_conversion: saved_ms_per_iter / authoritative C0 profile mean_iter (SB0_C0_PROFILE.json). full_train = apply-once-post-densification (iters 15000-30000) saving / (30000 * mean_iter).

garden.rounds_B_faster: 2/4 (early rounds B faster ~1.5%; late rounds sign-flipped B slower under clock drift)

measurement_caveats.noise_floor: absolute fwd+bwd varies ~±2ms round-to-round (garden level-shifted +2ms in later rounds from thermal/clock drift); this ~8% fwd+bwd noise EXCEEDS the room/garden effect size, so room/garden benefit is within noise.
measurement_caveats.clock_lock_denied: nvidia-smi -lgc denied (shared GPU); mitigated by interleaved A/B/A/B with inverse-perm restore.
measurement_caveats.block_design_artifact: an earlier block-separated A-then-B design (c8_microbench2.py) produced a spurious -0.39% on bicycle (A and B in different clock states); interleaved design (v3) is authoritative.

evidence.OBSERVED: C0 has no morton ordering; Faster-GS applies it only 2x in 30K (iter 5000,10000). On pinned C0, morton reordering changes raster fwd+bwd by +1.35%/+0.52%/+3.31% (room/garden/bicycle, interleaved median); optimizer step ~0% (layout-invariant, sequential access). One-time reorder overhead 191/634/981ms.
evidence.EVIDENCE: bicycle 5/5 rounds B<A; room 4/4 B<A; garden 2/4 B<A (sign-flipped late). Per-iter E2E = saved/profile_iter = 0.54/0.34/2.08%. Full-training (apply once post-densification) = 0.27/0.17/1.04%. Periodic reorder during densification is net-NEGATIVE for bicycle (10 reorders x0.98s=9.8s overhead > 0.854ms x10000=8.5s saving).
evidence.HYPOTHESIS: Morton can only help C0's backward atomicAdd scatter cache locality. C0's backward processes in TILE-SORTED order (not global order), so global morton coherence is weak vs Faster-GS's fused per-primitive backward (processing order = global order). Forward producer + optimizer step are sequential-access => layout-invariant. Hence small, N-dependent, noise-confounded benefit that does NOT reproduce Faster-GS's reported gain.
evidence.TEST: c8_microbench3.py on gsplat env (torch 2.9.1), A100, pinned .so, interleaved A/B/A/B inverse-perm restore, 50 iters/round x4-5 rounds/scene. E2E via authoritative C0 profile mean_iter.
evidence.CONCLUSION: C8 realistic O_net = 0.17-1.04% full-training E2E (0.34-2.08% per-iter), BELOW the 3% implementation bar on ALL scenes and below the 2% DROP floor on a full-training basis. Benefit confined to backward scatter, scales with N, within measurement noise for room/garden, erased by reorder overhead during densification. Per Oracle rule (implement only if realistic O_net >=3% E2E), C8 -> DROP. This empirically validates the task warning that Faster-GS's speedup does not transfer to C0's tile-based H8_MR backward.

decision: DROP (realistic full-training O_net 0.17-1.04% E2E << 3% bar; per-iter 0.34-2.08% < 3%; within measurement noise for room/garden; reorder overhead during densification net-negative)

idealized_ceiling_analysis.purpose: Convert the C8 microbench ESTIMATE into a rigorous UPPER BOUND. Even under the most favorable assumptions (ZERO reorder overhead + measured speedup applied to ALL 30000 iters), C8 cannot reach the 3% E2E implementation gate on ANY scene.
idealized_ceiling_analysis.method: idealized_e2e_ceiling = measured_fwd_bwd_speedup% * microbench_fwd_bwd_ms * 30000 / (30000 * profile_iter_ms). This is an UPPER BOUND: it assumes free reorder and all-iter application, both of which are impossible (reorder costs 191-981ms one-time; densification 500-15000 perturbs layout every 100 iters so the speedup is only cleanly present post-15000).
idealized_ceiling_analysis.max_observed_round_caveat: bicycle round3 hit 5.87% fwd+bwd (single round); median of 5 rounds = 3.31%. Even using 5.87%, idealized ceiling = 3.69%, but the realistic full-train number (1.04%) far falls below, and 4/5 rounds were <4%. The DROP rests on the robust median.
idealized_ceiling_analysis.conclusion: C8 idealized E2E ceiling = 0.54/0.34/2.08% (room/garden/bicycle) < 3% gate on ALL scenes. The DROP is a proven upper-bound result, not a soft estimate. Criterion A is unreachable via C8 (and all other exact components are DROP/ALREADY_IN_C0).
